policy: No standalone protocol may be added unless the Protocol Addition Gate passes. Existing protocols must absorb compatible requirements instead of creating duplicates.

protocols.name: Master Execution Contract
protocols.invariant: Execution remains non-terminal until required work, evidence, tests and root causes are closed.

protocols.name: Zero False Green
protocols.invariant: PASS requires complete fresh evidence on the exact tested SHA with no masking or partial execution.

protocols.name: Protocol Hierarchy & Conflict Resolution
protocols.invariant: Lower-level rules cannot weaken higher-level safety or product invariants.

protocols.name: Root-Cause-First Repair
protocols.invariant: Every persistent failure is repaired at its causal source and closed with five proofs.

protocols.name: Change-Scope Integrity
protocols.invariant: Declared affected scope is complete and cannot be shrunk or expanded to evade failure.

protocols.name: Dependency-Graph Closure
protocols.invariant: Local regression cannot close a repair while downstream contract nodes remain unverified.

protocols.name: Regression-First
protocols.invariant: A causal repair has a targeted regression proving pre-repair failure and post-repair correctness.

protocols.name: Canonical Test Ownership
protocols.invariant: Each canonical assertion has exactly one execution owner.

protocols.name: Test Deduplication & Value
protocols.invariant: Duplicate execution is consolidated without deleting required contract coverage.

protocols.name: Determinism & Flake Classification
protocols.invariant: Deterministic failures are repaired; retries cannot convert defects into PASS.

protocols.name: Cross-Browser Parity
protocols.invariant: Required browser engines execute equivalent required contract surfaces.

protocols.name: Route × Locale × Browser Matrix
protocols.invariant: Required public route/locale/browser units are complete, disjointly owned and evidenced.

protocols.name: Browser Runtime Failure Attribution
protocols.invariant: Application, console, network, navigation, browser and infrastructure failures remain distinguishable.

protocols.name: Single Source of Truth & Parity
protocols.invariant: Authoritative registry and all dependent surfaces remain 100% coherent.

protocols.name: Ready-State Integrity
protocols.invariant: Not-ready tools cannot be exposed as production-ready routes.

protocols.name: Localization & SEO Runtime Integrity
protocols.invariant: Runtime localized UI, SEO metadata, canonical routes and hreflang remain authoritative and consistent.

protocols.name: Evidence Freshness & Provenance
protocols.invariant: Primary evidence is bound to exact SHA, run, contract/version, inputs, runtime and artifact identity.

protocols.name: Evidence-to-Assertion Traceability
protocols.invariant: Every certified PASS traces from assertion through execution and artifact to the certified SHA.

protocols.name: Immutable Artifact & CI Critical Path
protocols.invariant: Build/install work is reused safely and duplicate execution does not inflate the critical path.

protocols.name: Agent Ownership, Continuity & Handoff
protocols.invariant: Mutable scopes have one owner and successors continue from fresh exact-SHA handoff state.
